```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
```

jellyqda is a small tool for **qualitative data analysis** of interview
transcripts and field notes -- deductive and inductive, e.g. qualitative
content analysis after Mayring or Kuckartz. It runs **entirely offline** on
your own computer: no account, no cloud, no upload. All project data lives in
**one SQLite file per project** (`.jellyqda`).

You can work in two ways that share the same project file:

* the **app** (`qda_app()`), a local web interface in the browser or the
  RStudio Viewer, available in English and German, and
* the **R functions** shown below, which make every step scriptable and
  reproducible.

## A project in a few lines

```{r}
library(jellyqda)
qda_language("en")                                 # report language (also: "de")

project <- file.path(tempfile(), "example.jellyqda")
qda_open(project)                                  # creates the project file

files <- system.file("extdata", c("interview_01.txt", "interview_02.md"),
                     package = "jellyqda")
qda_import(files, segments = "speaker")            # text is frozen on import
```

Imported text is **frozen** into the database and never extracted again, so
the character offsets of codings can never drift.

## Codes and subcodes

Codes form a tree. A subcode takes the colour of its code family; the app
draws subcodes as outlined boxes hanging on a coloured line ("thread").

```{r}
qda_code_add("Career path", color = "#E69F00")
qda_code_add("SME", parent = "Career path")
qda_code_add("Motivation", color = "#56B4E9")
qda_code_guide("SME",
  definition = "Statements about working in a small or medium-sized enterprise",
  rule = "Only explicit statements")
qda_codes()[, c("label", "path", "color")]
```

## Coding

A passage is addressed by its segment number (see `qda_view()`) or by
character offsets.

```{r}
qda_code(source = 1, segment = 2, code = "SME", memo = "first job")
qda_code(source = 1, start = 10, end = 60, code = "Motivation")
qda_autocode("project", code = "Career path", scope = "segment")
qda_codings()[, c("id", "source", "code", "start", "end")]
```

Every change is recorded in an audit trail and can be undone:

```{r}
qda_coding_recode(1, "Career path")
qda_undo()
qda_codings()$code[1]
```

## Memos and Mayring's summarising content analysis

```{r}
qda_memo_add("Ask about question 3 again", title = "Research diary")
qda_coding_set_summary(1, paraphrase = "Started in a small company",
                       generalization = "Career start in an SME")
qda_codings()[1, c("code", "paraphrase", "generalization")]
```

## Analysis

```{r}
qda_stats()$overall[, c("n_sources", "n_codes", "n_codings", "pct_coded")]
qda_matrix()
qda_words(n = 5)
qda_kwic("Projektleiterin", width = 25)[, c("source", "left", "match", "right")]
qda_source_set_var(1, "role", "project lead")
qda_case_matrix("role")
```

## Export, report and backup

`qda_export()` writes CSV, Excel and Word files and a standalone HTML report
into `exports/` next to the project. The report is made for printing on A4:
colours only appear as lines and borders, and a margin column next to each
interview shows which codings, comments and memos are at which place.

```{r}
out <- qda_export(c("codebook", "report"))
basename(out$file)
basename(qda_backup(quiet = TRUE))
```

## The app

```{r, eval = FALSE}
qda_app()               # language follows qda_language() / your system
qda_app(lang = "de")    # German user interface
```

In the app you mark text with the mouse and click a code; codes with
subcodes unfold them in the coding bar. The code tree supports "+ Code",
"+ Subcode", renaming by double click, merging codes and a coding guideline
per code. The analysis window offers word frequencies, keyword in context and
a table for Mayring's paraphrase and generalisation.

```{r, include = FALSE}
qda_close()
```

## Offline guarantee

jellyqda never opens a network connection; the app binds to `127.0.0.1`
only. The test suite checks the package source for network calls.
